summary: Frontend-only test of batch: theme grid removed from Settings, default-theme-select (admin), new sound packs Néant/Glacier/Neptune, theme card effects on creation page (detail-poster + MovixSelector cards) via CSS variables, Home regression. All functional checks that could be executed PASSED. The only problem: headless Chromium crashed ('Target crashed') on most page loads with theme=neptune (8 of 10 tries, on /, /parametres and /oeuvre/:id). The crash is intermittent: it also happened once with every animation/filter/blend/mask disabled, and other themes (abysse, glacier, neant, biome, monolithe, yorha) never crashed. No pageerrors on Home, /parametres or /oeuvre/:id. The only console error is a React hydration warning ('<span> cannot be a child of <option>') in the CommentsSection select; it comes from the Emergent visual-edit instrumentation wrapping {expr} in <option>, not from the app.

ui_bugs.issue: Headless Chromium renderer crashes ~1s after load with sx_theme=neptune on /parametres, / and /oeuvre/:id (8/10 attempts). It worked 2 times: Detail page once, and /parametres once with a style that disabled animation/filter/mask/blend. It crashed again with that same override later, so the root cause is not proven. Overriding only the new neptune card vars (--card-an/--fx-an/--fx-bl/--fx-bg) did not stop the crash, so it is probably not the new card-effect block. It may only affect headless/software-GL, but worth checking the neptune GPU load (animated masks/gradients, bubbles, jelly SVG, CyberOverlay scan) on low-end devices.

action_items: Look into the Neptune theme renderer crash in headless Chromium (repeatable on fresh load). Profile the neptune background/overlay layers (animated masks, repeating gradients, bubbles, jelly SVG) and reduce GPU cost if possible.
Give Neptune its own CyberOverlay READOUT (it currently shows 'ABYSSE').
Optional: fix the <option> children in CommentsSection select (use a template string) to silence the hydration warning.
critical_code_review_comments: sound.js out(): the echo feedback loop (d->lp->fb->d) is only partly disconnected after 3s (g and d). lp/fb nodes stay referenced until GC. This is fine, but each UI sound builds a new delay graph, so heavy hovering creates many nodes. Consider one shared echo bus per pack.
Settings.js UiSoundPicker plays a hover sound on every mouseenter of every pack card. Fine, but throttle it to avoid stacked graphs.
